newsitem.title: USA: IMF delays release of loan to Kenya.
newsitem.headline: IMF delays release of loan to Kenya.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund has delayed the release of $36 million to Kenya because of concerns about its handling of a multi-million dollar financial scandal, IMF officials said on Monday.

The officials, who declined to be named, said the IMF had given the Kenyan government until the end of July to respond to its concerns or face the potential suspension of its Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF) loan agreement.
"Unless the (IMF) board receives a satisfactory response to these questions, it is unlikely the mid-term review of the first annual ESAF (loan) will be completed," an official said.

The delay in disbursement of the loan -- it had originally been slated for approval at the end of last month -- was a blow to Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi at a time of mounting protests inside the country against his rule.
At least seven people were killed on Monday when police broke up protests against Moi, badly beating organisers of the opposition-backed rallies and firing into the crowds.

The IMF move followed a June 20 decision by the high court in Nairobi to end prosecution of former government officials and a businessman allegedly involved in the financial scandal. The Kenyan government has appealed the decision.

The scandal involves Goldenberg International, a firm that was paid millions of dollars under an export compensation scheme for diamond and gold exports. Kenya produces little gold and has no diamond deposits.

An IMF official said the fund's board wanted the Kenyan government to clarify what measures it planned to take to counter the "irregularities" that made the Goldenberg scheme possible and when it planned to take them.
The board also wanted to know what the government of the East African nation would do to recover the "rather large" amount of money it lost as a result of the Goldenberg case, the official added.
The $36 million is part of a $216 million ESAF credit approved for Kenya in April 1996. The IMF has already handed over $36 million to Kenya under that loan agreement.
